claims.statement: KAS reports over 3.2 million registered heavy vehicles, about 5,870 kilometres of paid roads and a legal obligation for vehicles over 3.5 tonnes and buses using covered roads to pay through e-TOLL.
KAS changed heavy-vehicle rates from 1 January 2026, and its classifier states that the rate depends on vehicle mass category, emission class and road class.
Reconciling tolls to dispatch and telematics may expose errors or route savings, but total registered vehicles are not the same as an affordably reachable paying market.
The incidence and recoverable value of overcharges or preventable exceptions in 10-to-200-vehicle fleets is unknown.

contrary_evidence: KAS provides a free driver app and account portal, while EETS and telematics providers already combine toll services for many fleets.
A cheaper toll route can cost more in fuel, driver time or delivery performance, so optimization must model total trip economics.
The reported 3.2 million registered vehicles describe system scale, not unique active customers or accessible SMEs.

economics.acquisition_route: Embed with OBU and ZSL providers, fuel-card issuers, transport accountants and telematics integrators; sell first as an audit report through partners rather than another driver app.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A route-section, vehicle, rate, device-state and confirmed-anomaly dataset can make reconciliation faster and reveal recurring issues by hardware or fleet workflow.
fingerprint.customer: Polish road hauliers, bus operators and field-service fleets with roughly 10 to 200 heavy vehicles that already use an OBU or external location system but reconcile tolls manually.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed with OBU and ZSL providers, fuel-card issuers, transport accountants and telematics integrators; sell first as an audit report through partners rather than another driver app.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Reconcile dispatch and telematics tracks against e-TOLL notes, verify vehicle and emission-class masters, alert on data gaps or unusual charges, simulate route toll cost alongside time and fuel, and assemble a traceable claim pack for human submission.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The fleet pays tolls as trips occur and reconciles them monthly. Charge per vehicle per month for anomaly and route-cost control, with a separate success fee only for verified refunds or avoided misclassification.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Every trip over the paid network generates a per-kilometre charge based on vehicle category and emission class; device outages, vehicle-master errors, route deviations, low prepaid balance or rate changes create exceptions, administrative risk or avoidable cost.

founder_fit: Quantitative reconciliation and anomaly detection match the founder's data-science skills.
Poland supplies a focused regulatory wedge with a large recorded vehicle base.
Telematics partners can provide scalable distribution without camera-based marketing.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: e-TOLL reconciliation and route-cost control for Polish fleets
uncertainties: Billing-data export or API availability and partner permissioning.
Frequency of vehicle-master, route and device anomalies that lead to money recovery rather than only alerts.
Partner revenue share and support cost per vehicle.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Run a three-month read-only reconciliation over at least 20 fleets and one million vehicle-kilometres, classify every mismatch and verify each with the fleet before assigning value. Pre-sell through one OBU or accounting partner only if verified annual recovery plus admin savings exceeds three times the proposed annual subscription.
